scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8058: Hello, I'm on PC5 in Campus 1 (the 172.16.10.x group).
I can't reach the design group's machines upstairs (the 172.16.30.x ones) any
more -- they all time out for me. People in my own group are reachable just
fine. I don't understand how the floors are joined up, sorry. Could someone
have a look and fix whatever is broken between us? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. mswitch0 owns the L3 SVIs for VLAN 10/20/30
  (172.16.10.254 / 172.16.20.254 / 172.16.30.254) and routes between them; a
  VLAN 10 host reaches a VLAN 30 host with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / inter-VLAN
  fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 30 within Campus 1 -- is NOT reproducible: mswitch0's SVIs (172.16.10.254,
172.16.30.254) are up, and a VLAN 10 host (PC5) reaches a VLAN 30 host
(172.16.30.x) with 0% loss via mswitch0.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing on mswitch0 is
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
VLAN10->VLAN30 path, finds it working, checks the SVIs on mswitch0, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a down/misconfigured SVI to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough end-to-end investigation of the VLAN 10 ↔ VLAN 30 inter-VLAN path found no fault at any layer. The relevant data path runs from pc5 (172.16.10.5, VLAN 10 access port on switch1) through an 802.1Q trunk to mswitch0, which performs inter-VLAN routing via Linux bridge VLAN subinterfaces (vlan10@br0 at 172.16.10.254 and vlan30@br0 at 172.16.30.254), then down a VLAN-30 trunk through switch3 to the destination hosts (pc12–pc14, 172.16.30.12–.14).

Every component was verified in both directions:
- pc5 successfully pinged all three VLAN-30 hosts (172.16.30.12, .13, .14) with zero packet loss.
- pc12 and pc13 successfully pinged back to 172.16.10.5 and 172.16.10.6 with zero packet loss.
- mswitch0's FRR OSPF config correctly advertises 172.16.10.0/24 and 172.16.30.0/24 with both subnets present as directly-connected routes in the FIB.
- iptables, ebtables, and nftables on mswitch0 and switch3 all show empty ACCEPT policies — no access-control rules exist.
- switch1 and switch3 bridges are correctly configured with VLAN subinterfaces on their uplinks, and all access ports are UP and forwarding.
- router16 (upstream to mswitch0) has a clean OSPF config with no ACLs.

The symptom described in the helpdesk ticket does not correspond to any fault present in the lab. The network between VLAN 10 (172.16.10.x) and VLAN 30 (172.16.30.x) is fully operational. No corrective action is needed; the ticket should be closed as a false alarm or the reporter asked to re-test from their actual workstation.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states mswitch0 has vlan10@br0 (172.16.10.254) and vlan30@br0 (172.16.30.254) and shows successful inter-VLAN pings and correct directly-connected routes, confirming SVIs up and baseline routing healthy.
